title: Competing with big companies: go where gorillas can't follow and do what they can't
summary: Jason Cohen argues founders overfear the 800-lb gorilla. Big companies are slow, only play in big markets, and are boxed in by their brand and existing revenue, so a small company can use their entry to validate its market, pick niches they ignore, and win by doing what they structurally cannot. The more dangerous rival is another scrappy startup.

principles.text: Fear the nimble small startup copying you more than the slow incumbent, who will likely be doing the same thing in two to four years.
principles.quote: What *is* scary is another scrappy, smart startup like yours--another tree-shrew. The one who silently observes you from afar, then drives down the road you paved, skipping the mistakes you made and copying the good parts.

principles.text: Your goal is to earn more customers on your own terms, not to beat or destroy another company.
principles.quote: **It's not your purpose to "beat" another company.** It's your purpose to define yourself on your own terms, not in terms of how you're like or unlike someone else.

principles.text: A big player entering your market validates it and can raise your company's value, since their rivals then need an answer.
principles.quote: In short, Microsoft copying the idea would only validate the market, causing the value of Smart Bear to increase.

principles.text: Big companies only play in big markets, so pick a market worth about $100M that they can't justify entering, but not a micro-niche.
principles.quote: Big companies play only in big markets.

principles.text: A big company's strengths (brand, customer base, revenue stream) also restrict it: it can't take risks, ship quickly, or change its image.
principles.quote: They can't take a risk because protecting the existing revenue stream is more important than *anything* else, even if it means their ultimate demise.

principles.text: Do what incumbents can't: change the product, fill the image gap, and act on customer feedback within a week.
principles.quote: They can't change their product, so you can innovate without competition. They can't change their image, so you can fill the gap. They can't listen to a customer and make an impact one week later; you can.
